game.title: Resident Evil 2 (2019 remake)
game.build_notes: Verified 2026-09-04 on the Steam build with REFramework rev 76298bd (pd-upscaler fork, 2026-03-11) installed as dinput8.dll. The game runs WINDOWED on this machine (1920x1421 client area at screen offset 768,31); all captures are BitBlt of that client rectangle after SetForegroundWindow. The REFramework overlay opens on every boot and is closed with INSERT before anything else; keyboard input still reaches the game while it is open, mouse does not.

input.api: Win32 keyboard via REFramework's hooked message loop reaches the game; mouse buttons do NOT arrive through SendInput (see disproved binding). Gamepad untested.
input.api_notes: SendInput with SCANCODES works for every keyboard key tried. Numpad keys must be sent by VIRTUAL KEY (wVk 0x60+n, no SCANCODE flag): a numpad scancode with NumLock off reports as HOME/END/PGUP to GetAsyncKeyState, so a plugin polling VK_NUMPADn never sees it. Mouse: MOUSEEVENTF_RIGHTDOWN/RIGHTUP via SendInput produced no aim (SurvivorCondition.IsHold stayed false through a 2 s hold, twice); the engine appears to take mouse buttons from a path SendInput does not feed. Use the game's own input system instead (see commands).

bindings.notes: The menu footer says 'Space: Confirm'. Return is the right mouse button, so there is no keyboard 'back' proven yet; ESC untested.

Synthetic right-mouse via SendInput never raised IsHold. Aim is reachable natively: app.ropeway.InputSystem.setForce(64 /*HOLD*/, true) from a REFramework plugin or Lua raises the full aim state (animation bank, IsHold) and setForce(64,false) drops it cleanly.
Overlay is OPEN at every boot on this install. Close it first: it swallows mouse input while open.

commands.notes: No console. The game's own input system is scriptable through REFramework: app.ropeway.InputSystem (managed singleton) .setForce(kind, bool) with kind HOLD=64 and ATTACK=256 (app.ropeway.InputDefine.Kind). Verified live 2026-09-04 from a native plugin: setForce(64,true) -> SurvivorCondition.IsHold true within a frame, aim animation bank engaged; setForce(64,false) -> back to locomotion. The same call was proven from Lua on 2026-08-27. Managed state (player, weapon, motion layers) is readable through REFramework's TDB reflection; the Visceral repo's dev-archive/plugin is a worked example.

hazards.hazard: REFramework overlay opens at boot and eats mouse input while open; keyboard still passes.
The Continue save lands next to a typewriter with its prompt active; an interact press opens the save UI.

Invoking System.GC.KeepAlive (an internal call with no resolvable body in this build) through REFramework's reflection crashes the game about 8 s later inside the native invoker. Hooking it fails first ('Failed to hook … unknown exception'). Use compiled app.ropeway.* methods as hook targets.
Synthetic mouse buttons via SendInput do not reach the game (no aim on RMB).
The plugin DLL cannot be redeployed while the game runs (file locked); every plugin change costs a graceful close, copy, relaunch and the title-to-save route (~90 s).

Weapon selection from the inventory is NOT automated yet (no proven key route into the inventory grid and onto 'Equip'); the Continue save lands on the minigun, and a handgun run needed a human to equip it before walking away.
